_rule: Round 5 of the filing readings (decision rules of 23 October 2026, a decision of the Claude analysis session, results/extraction_error_rate/mature-cohort/round5/rules.md). 'excluded' (rule 1): a record leaves the PRIMARY sample (outcome 'mature_cohort') when its year t development table's history (an underwriting year u <= t-2, or the table as a whole) differs from the year t-1 report beyond the exchange rate with no explanation in either filing; AND the year t table fails the year's accounts (implied gross incurred, or paid where computable, off by more than 10% beyond what its basis explains) while the year t-1 control ties within 5%; AND the year t-1 report's printed base does not give a figure that reconciles either. The loader (run_analysis.py) removes an 'excluded' entry's record at the unusable-severity step with the tag RESTATED_BASE_TABLE and counts it (restated_base_excluded); under outcome 'precedence_672' the register is not read and nothing changes. 'history_restated' (rule 6): the table ties to the year's accounts (or its basis explains the gap), but an underwriting year u <= t-2 moved beyond the exchange rate without explanation by more than 1% of R (unexplained_history_move), or the two readings disagree on the validity label (valid, screen_misread, units_slip against restated_base, undeterminable) but not on the facts (label_disagreement), or (rule 5b) the filing prints no transferred gross amount for a take-on in year t but bounds it at or below 10% of R (take_on_base_bounded), or an explained take-on already in R has a table that does not reconcile with the filing's own roll-forward (take_on_table_unreconciled); the record stays in the primary and src/check_low_confidence_sensitivity.py leaves it out of its least-certain refit. 'takeon_unmeasurable' (rule 5b, decision of the Claude analysis session, 23 October 2026): a record leaves the PRIMARY sample when an RITC, LPT or merger effective in year t, whose acquired history the table shows as if always, is not in the opening gross claims outstanding R, the filing does not print the transferred gross reserves, and the readings show the acquired share of the base could exceed 10% of R (an unmeasurable take-on, as 1861/2020 and 1084/2022 are); the loader removes the entry's record at the unusable-severity step with the tag TAKEON_BASE_UNMEASURABLE and counts it (takeon_base_unmeasurable_excluded); under outcome 'precedence_672' nothing changes. A take-on the filing bounds at or below 10% of R stays and is listed under history_restated. Every entry rests on two independent readings of the filing (and the tie-break readings where the first two disagreed on the facts), with the pages and quotes. Built by src/build_restated_base_excluded.py from the archived readings.

readings.note: Same basis, no explanation of the restatement anywhere in either filing. The 2023 table is an internally consistent restatement of the paid and incurred history of the 2020 and 2021 years (both inflated by about 97m in total versus the 2022 table and the 2023 accounts' paid/incurred flows) that leaves outstanding unchanged. M = +42.378m is therefore a difference of cumulative figures that the accounts' own gross flows (58.2m incurred, of which at most about 7m for the 2021-and-prior years) cannot support; and the 104m measured from the 2022 report's diagonal is worse. The 2023 net table (p47) shows the same restatement (2021 net one year later 94,274 and two years later 136,650, i.e. +42.4m in 2023 against the net 9.26m stated on p7). Neither the 2022 nor the 2023 report states what caused it. Not a 2023 transaction: no 2023 RITC or transfer; the only RITC (2019 and prior to Syndicate 1254, immediately after 31 December 2021) is in the 2022 opening balance and does not touch the 2020-2022 years. Whether the 2022 table or the 2023 table is the faulty one is not decidable from the pages, but the 2023 table does not tie to the 2023 flows. The 2023 table's M is not a genuine 2023 development of the 2020-2021 years.

rollforward_2023.agreement_with_M: M = +42,378 does not agree with a 2023 prior-year line of ~2.9m (closed-year) or 9.26m net (2021-and-prior YOA, p7). It also cannot fit inside total gross incurred: 58,191 less 2022-UY movement (63,498 - 33,254 = 30,244) less 2023 UY first-year (21,300) leaves about 6.6m for UYs 2020-2021 (derived, residual; 7.1m with the 447 FX). The 104m measured from the 2022 diagonal is impossible (it exceeds total gross incurred of 58.2m). Table movements in 2023 sum to 2,881 + 39,497 + 30,244 + 21,300 = 93,922 vs 58,191 gross incurred, a 35.7m excess sitting in the 2020-21 rows; net table movements 4,228 + 42,376 + 30,600 + 18,258 = 95,462 vs net incurred 55,377 (excess 40.1m). By contrast the 2023 UY (net 18,258 vs 18,248 p7) and 2022 UY (net 30,600 vs 27,870 p7) rows tie closely to the calendar-year table, so the excess is in the 2020-21 rows. The 2020 gross row movement (+2,881) does match the printed '$2.9m deterioration on closed year reserves' (p47), which points to 2020 being a true 2023 movement and the 2021 +39,497 (restated base) being the problem row.

readings.true_movement_notes: The filing does not print a gross 2020-21 movement. Indicators: (a) gross 2020 row +2.881m equals the printed '$2.9m deterioration on closed year reserves' (p47); (b) net calendar-year claims incurred on 2021-and-prior YOA 9.26m (p7), which includes current-year exposure; (c) derived residual of total gross incurred 58.191m less 2022-UY row 30.244m less 2023-UY 21.300m = about 6.6m for UYs 2020-21 together. So the true 2023 gross development of 2020-21 is of order 3m to 9m, not 42.4m and not 104m. These are my derivations from printed lines, not a figure the filing states.
readings.note: Both tables carry the same heading and basis wording, both reconcile to their balance-sheet gross claims outstanding, and no restatement note or 2023 transaction exists, so presentation alone is not explained; yet the 2023 table's historical incurred and paid cells for UYs 2020-21 are higher than the 2022 print by amounts that net to zero in outstanding (end-2022 incurred 253,729 vs 192,060; paid implied 144,792 vs 83,123), and the 2023 table's year-on-year movement exceeds the 2023 income statement's total gross incurred by 35.7m. M = +42.378m therefore rests on a rebased history (largely the 2021 column, +39.5m) that is not 2023 development, and using the 2022 diagonal (104m) is worse. Not an RITC/transfer (none in 2023). Possible 'development' reading is not supported by the income statement tie-out. The paid history is also unexplained: the 2023 table's cumulative paid rose 133,076 across 2020-2023 rows vs gross claims paid of 36,123 in 2023, on the 2022 base; so the filings contain an unexplained inconsistency in the earlier years of the table. Recommend excluding or treating as undeterminable-for-M-size if a conservative rule is preferred; my reading is restated_base.

explanation.stated_in_2017: p24: 'Historic development includes a mix of prior year releases and deteriorations, and in 2017 gross and net deteriorations occurred.' p5: 'A strengthening of prior period reserves' and 'The partial recovery of the value of Sterling against the US Dollar' as drivers of 2017.
explanation.syndicate_958: 2017 p5: 'With effect from the 2016 year of account, CMA merged Syndicate 958's capacity into Syndicate 4444. The 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 will be reinsured to close into Syndicate 4444, effective from 1 January 2018.' 2017 p7 (future developments): 'At 31 December 2017, Syndicate 4444 accepted the reinsurance to close for the 2015 year of account of Syndicate 958, its final underwriting year.' The 2018 report settles the timing: p17 'With effect from 1 January 2018 the 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 has been reinsured to close (RITC'd) into Syndicate 4444. The financial statements include the RITC of syndicate 958, 2017 comparatives for syndicate 4444 are pre the RITC.' So the RITC is not in the 2017 table or accounts (and p7's 'At 31 December 2017' wording is a signing date, not a recognition date). The 2016 merger of 958's capacity affects the 2016 year of account onward, not the 2011-2015 columns. Nothing in either filing links the RITC to the end-2016 history of the 2017 table.
explanation.fx: No exchange rate is printed. Direction from the filing: 2017 p5 lists 'the partial recovery of the value of Sterling against the US Dollar' (Sterling stronger: US dollar amounts become fewer pounds); US dollar technical provisions are 1,227,673 of 2,003,465 = 61% (2017 p31). The accounts' own translation effect on gross claims outstanding in 2017 is a reduction of 33,144 (balance sheet movement 346,658 less change in provision 379,802, p13/p16), 2.8% of the opening 1,200,561. So a stronger Sterling should lower the end-2016 cells in the 2017 table; they are 4.7% (2011, 2012) and 3.9% (2013) HIGHER and only 2014-2016 are within a few percent. In the control year the cells moved with the currency: the 2016 table's end-2015 cells are 2.3% to 10.7% higher than the 2015 print (2011 351,980 vs 344,242 = 1.0225; 2012 363,811 vs 351,920 = 1.0338; 2013 372,441 vs 356,540 = 1.0446; 2014 385,327 vs 360,033 = 1.0703; 2015 240,706 vs 217,535 = 1.1065), in a year the 2016 report describes as 'a fall in the value of Sterling against the US Dollar following the UK's decision to leave the European Union' (2016 p5). That is the direction an FX rise would give, and the size is plausible for the share of US dollar business. 2017 moves the other way in the old years, so currency does not explain it.

readings.explanation: No stated restatement of the claims history. Searched the 2017 report for restat / re-present / reclass / prior period / correction / change in accounting: only p21 'Previously, overseas deposits were included in the Statement of Cashflows ... The 2016 comparatives have also been prepared using this presentational basis' (cash flow presentation, not claims). The 2016 report's 'restated' items (p16, p28, p29, p31) are 2015 comparatives of investments and Lloyd's reporting, not claims. 2017 p25 says only: 'The tables below are presented at the exchange rates prevailing at 31 December 2017. ... Historic development includes a mix of prior year releases and deteriorations, and in 2017 gross and net deteriorations occurred.' (same table wording as 2016 p24 apart from the deterioration sentence). p5 strategic report: 'A strengthening of prior period reserves'. Note 24 p42 gross claims: 'At 1 January 1,200,561; Increase/ (decrease) in provision 379,802; Foreign exchange (70,340); Other 37,196; At 31 December 1,547,219' (2016: 912,779; 166,053; 121,533; 196). The 'Other 37,196' (no reinsurers' share) is not explained anywhere in the filing.
readings.transaction: p5: 'With effect from the 2016 year of account, CMA merged Syndicate 958's capacity into Syndicate 4444. The 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 will be reinsured to close into Syndicate 4444, effective from 1 January 2018.' p7: 'At 31 December 2017, Syndicate 4444 accepted the reinsurance to close for the 2015 year of account of Syndicate 958, its final underwriting year.' Effective date 1 Jan 2018 supports 'not in the 2017 figures', but the contract was accepted on 31 Dec 2017 and note 3d p19 says an accepted RITC's 'premium ... is recognised as income in the financial year that the RITC contract is signed, together with related claims liabilities'. I found no RITC premium or claims line in the 2017 accounts, so I cannot confirm or exclude that the unexplained 'Other 37,196' is connected. Not decisive for the base comparison (a 2018 effective RITC would not alter the end-2016 diagonal).

readings.reconciliation_of_2016_base_to_2017_acco: No. Latest 2017 cells less the 2016 printed base give 1,112.6m (+10.3%) or 1,169.3m (+15.9% with 2010&prior) against gross incurred of 1,008.5m, and the gap widens once the base is retranslated to end-2017 rates. readings.verdict_detail: The 2017 table's end-2016 history is not the 2016 report's history and the change is not explained. Individual cells move by up to +4.7% (older years) and -22.5% (2015 at age 0), outside the range sterling retranslation can produce (+3.5% to -8.1% per the p36 rates) and opposite in sign to the dominant US-dollar effect, and the ratio rises smoothly with age rather than being constant per currency mix. The filing states no restatement, correction or change of basis. The incurred test misses 5% (+6.3% against a -1.1% control), the paid proxy is +30.8% (control -6.2%; mixed-base because the 2017 table prints no end-2016 payments), and the claims reconciliation carries an unexplained 'Other 37,196'. The Syndicate 958 RITC is effective 1 Jan 2018 (p5), so it is unlikely to be in the end-2016 cells, but acceptance on 31 Dec 2017 (p7) and the unexplained 'Other' leave a small unresolved doubt. The movement is not measurable from the table with confidence: M is +118.2m on the 2017 table's own cells and +167.7m on the 2016 printed base (u 2011-2015), a 29% spread, and the filing prints no gross mature-cohort movement. 'Valid' (stated adverse development) is right about the sign (p25: 'in 2017 gross and net deteriorations occurred') but not about the base.
readings.note: Why not valid: criteria need the table to tie to the accounts (incurred within 5%) and any history change explained or immaterial; neither holds. Why not stronger than moderate: the history change is small (1.8% of the diagonal, 3.4% of opening reserves), the table's balance to pay ties exactly to the balance sheet, the own-cell incurred miss is only 6.3%, and the incurred test is blunt here (basis-adjusted control -8.1%). If the analysis keeps the record it should use the table's own two diagonals (+118.2m) and flag the sensitivity to the 2016 base (+167.7m); the author should decide. Same age-dependent drift appears (smaller) from the 2015 report to the 2016 table (end-2015 cells 1.023, 1.034, 1.045, 1.070, 1.107 times the 2015 latest), where the US dollar rose against sterling (FX ceiling far larger), so that year is consistent with FX.

1110_2022.facts: rule 5b (U1, U2; P7, Q6 for the table). The Syndicate 5678 RITC (all open years of account, the 2018 and 2019 underwriting years named; agreement of 9 February 2022, p5, p33) and an INWARD adverse development cover for certain years of Syndicates 33 and 3624 (the Hiscox ADC, p5): 1110 is the reinsurer, so both add gross reserves; the Gibson Re 80% whole account quota share is outward and moves the reinsurers' share, not the gross reserves. The filing prints no transferred gross amount: note 3's gross roll-forward (p27) has no transfer row (221,885 + claims incurred 353,805 - paid 99,706 + foreign exchange 13,619 = 489,603, GBP 000), so the take-on sits inside claims incurred, and gross written premium rose from 1.366m to 333.442m, mainly on the two deals (p6, p15). U2 derives a take-on of about 221.9m less the unknown development on the opening book, about 100% of R and about twice the base; closing reserves are 2.2 times the opening. The development table carries the acquired 2018 and 2019 years with their full history as if always (p37) and restates the older columns against the 2021 filing (U2), so the movement the table gives (+9.082m) is development on a combined book of about twice R. The acquired share of the base could exceed 10% of R by a wide margin and cannot be measured from the filing: the record leaves the primary

readings.note: Two points. (1) The screen's 'units_case' is a screen misread: both reports are in £000 and the screen read the wrong 2021 page (p16) and label (millions, USD); no units slip in the filings, no scale effect on M. (2) The history in the 2022 table is a real, stated structural rebase: the 2022 RITC of Syndicate 5678's years and the Hiscox ADC bring about 270m of gross liabilities (closing claims outstanding 489.6m against 221.9m a year earlier) into columns for earlier underwriting years, and the table is a pro-forma combined book (cumulative paid history of the acquired books included). The year's accounts show the RITC/ADC through claims (353.8m gross incurred), which the table cannot reproduce (141.0m implied from its own diagonals), so the table is not tied to the year's accounts and the filing prints no stand-alone movement on the opening book. M = 9.1m therefore measures the 2022 development of the combined (opening plus acquired) book against a denominator R = 221.9m that covers only the opening book (the acquired liabilities are not in R); the same scale problem as 3500_2023. The explanation exists, so it is not a silent restatement; the figure is not a like-for-like prior-year movement on the opening reserves.

readings.basis: Gross of reinsurance, underwriting (year of account) ultimate-type estimates. Reserve ties: 442,381 + 47,223 = 489,604 = note 'At 31 December 2022 489,603'. The accounts' gross claims incurred of 353,805 include the take-on (segment note p26: Reinsurance class gross written premium 248,181 and gross claims incurred (263,083)); the table's opening cells are the combined book, so its implied incurred leaves the take-on out.
readings.note: A take-on, not an error: the 2022 table's end-2021 cells are not the syndicate's own end-2021 estimates (they carry Syndicate 5678's RITC'd years as if always, per the cell jumps) and the table's implied incurred (141.0m) is 60% below the accounts' gross incurred (353.8m) because the accounts book the RITC and ADC through premium and claims incurred. The table is arithmetically sound (reserve ties to the balance sheet) and M inside it is +9.08m, but that is development on the combined book including reserves acquired on 1 Jan 2022; it is not a movement on the syndicate's own opening reserves (221.9m gross), so M/R is inflated. Same family as 4000/2022 (RITC from Syndicate 3334) but here the accounts do not tie; treat as a transaction case for the author's scope decision. Unexplained: the common +8% on 2013, 2014 and 2020. Stored-grid label slip: 2021 grid says USD/millions on p16; the filing is GBP thousands on p28.
